data.title: Nigeria leads African bourses with 72% dollar gain as eight markets beat Wall Street
data.description:
Nigeria’s stock market is Africa’s best performer in dollar terms so far in 2026, with the NGX All-Share Index up 72.1% year to date in US dollars and 59.6% in naira. Many of the continent’s frontier markets are outpacing both Wall Street and emerging-market benchmarks, while South Africa and Morocco, two of Africa’s biggest markets, have fallen.

Of the 15 African indices for which data provider Mansa Markets publishes comparable dollar returns, eight have beaten the S&P 500’s 5.8% gain this year, based on Mansa’s calculations using closing prices for November 17-19. The iShares MSCI Emerging Markets ETF, which Mansa uses as its emerging-market benchmark, has risen 4.5% over the same period.

Tanzania’s Dar es Salaam Stock Exchange ranks second, up 48.4% in dollars and 59.4% in local currency, followed by the Ghana Stock Exchange at 47.2% (58.4% in cedi), the Rwanda Stock Exchange at 45.0% and the Uganda Securities Exchange at 38.1%. The BRVM, the Abidjan-based regional exchange for the eight member states of the West African Economic and Monetary Union, has gained 36.1% in dollars, and Kenya’s Nairobi Securities Exchange 28.0%.

The Zimbabwe Stock Exchange’s All Share Index has posted the biggest local-currency gain on the continent, at 77.0%, but Mansa Markets does not publish a comparable dollar return for it, so it is not included in the dollar ranking. Other providers do calculate one: Dabafinance put the Zimbabwe index up 63.6% in dollars in early October.

Nigeria has led in dollar terms for most of the year, apart from a spell in mid-year when Zimbabwe overtook it, BusinessDay reported. Its margin has narrowed since early October, when the NGX was up 76.1% in dollars and Tanzania’s exchange 56.8%, according to figures compiled by Dabafinance. The rally has also revived listings: 13 African IPOs have raised $1.9bn this year, the most since 2017, IntelliNews reported, citing Bloomberg data.

Nigeria’s rally faces year-end test

Nigerian analysts attribute the rally to currency stability, strong corporate earnings, easing inflation and interest rate cuts. The NGX Oil and Gas index had gained 125.9% this year by mid-September, with industrial goods up 81.6% and banking stocks 74.2%, BusinessDay reported. FTSE Russell reclassified Nigeria from unclassified to frontier status with effect from September 21, and S&P Dow Jones Indices has placed the country on its 2027 watch list for possible reclassification from standalone to frontier status. Analysts say the moves could support foreign portfolio inflows, though neither guarantees them.

So far the rally has been driven largely by local money: foreign portfolio investors were net sellers of Nigerian equities in each of the first eight months of the year, with net sales of NGN275.16bn over the period, IntelliNews has reported.

“As global capital re-engages with Nigeria, our focus at NGX is to ensure that investors have a market that is transparent,” Jude Chiemeka, chief executive of Nigerian Exchange Limited, told BusinessDay in September.

Brokers expect gains to slow. “I remain cautiously optimistic about the Nigerian stock market for the rest of the year,” Olatunde Amolegbe, managing director of Arthur Stevens Asset Management and immediate past president of the Chartered Institute of Stockbrokers, told Vanguard on November 9, adding that “some consolidation and profit-taking should be expected”.

He forecast a full-year return of about 57.7%, slightly below the index’s current gain. He cited high interest rates, exchange-rate uncertainty and caution among foreign portfolio investors ahead of the 2027 general elections as risks.

Others see the listing of Dangote Refinery as the main year-end driver. Its $1.6bn initial public offering, which closed on October 27, drew orders of about $4.78bn, IntelliNews reported. Sam Onukwue, managing director of Mega Equities, said that “with the listing of the Dangote Refinery IPO, market capitalization could cross the N200 trillion mark in December 2026”, up from about NGN162trn in September.

He blamed the market’s October weakness on the “migration of financial assets to Dangote Refinery IPO in the primary market” and expects the All-Share Index to end the year at about 280,000 points, Vanguard reported. The refinery’s shares have yet to begin trading.

Big markets lag

Some of Africa’s biggest and most established markets have trailed. South Africa’s JSE All Share Index is down 8.0% in rand terms and 9.8% in dollars, a reversal from early September, when it was up 5.2% in dollars, according to Dabafinance. Morocco’s MASI has fallen 9.8% in dirhams and 17.4% in dollars. Egypt’s EGX 30 has still beaten Wall Street, but a weaker pound has cut its 23.0% local-currency gain to 9.1% in dollars.

Malawi has posted the steepest decline this year, with its All Share Index down 19.9%. Mauritius and Botswana are also lower in dollar terms, while Zambia’s exchange is down 6.4% in kwacha but up 1.2% in dollars thanks to a firmer currency.

Standout stocks

Stock figures below are year-to-date share price changes in local currency (US dollars on the VFEX) to closes of November 19-20, compiled from exchange publications and from data sites AFX, African Financials, MarketScreener and BRVM Data. They exclude dividends, may not capture every small listed company and are not directly comparable with the dollar index returns above.

In Nigeria, the biggest gains among actively traded stocks have come from Berger Paints (NGX:BERGER), up 206% year to date at the November 19 close, UPDC REIT (NGX:UPDCREIT) and oil producer Seplat Energy (NGX:SEPLAT), both up 180%, Airtel Africa (NGX:AIRTELAFRI), up 176%, and HBM Nigeria (NGX:HBMNG), formerly Lafarge Africa, up 157%, according to prices compiled by data site AFX. Dangote Cement (NGX:DANGCEM), which has shelved a planned $1bn London listing, has gained 117% and Zenith Bank (NGX:ZENITHBANK) 84%, while Guaranty Trust Holding (NGX:GTCO) is up 28% and United Bank for Africa (NGX:UBA) is down 7%.

Some thinly traded Nigerian stocks show larger headline gains. SCOA Nigeria (NGX:SCOA) is up 365% and Union Dicon Salt (NGX:UNIONDICON) 244%, though both have barely traded since August. Shares in Fortis Global Insurance (NGX:FTGINSURE) appear to have risen almost ninefold, but the figure is distorted by a share reconstruction in June. Adjusted for it, the stock had gained 126% by the end of September, Nairametrics reported.

In Ghana, smaller stocks have led the rally. Cocoa Processing Company (GSE:CPC) is up 1,540% and Intravenous Infusions (GSE:IIL) 1,040%, though both started the year at the minimum price of GH¢0.05, which exaggerates percentage moves. Among more substantial companies, Clydestone (GSE:CLYD) is up 680%, SIC Insurance (GSE:SIC) 303%, Republic Bank Ghana (GSE:RBGH) 177%, Enterprise Group (GSE:EGL) 141% and Standard Chartered Bank Ghana (GSE:SCB) 139%, according to AFX data to November 19. GCB Bank (GSE:GCB) has gained 99% and MTN Ghana (GSE:MTNGH) 57%. Ecobank Transnational (GSE:ETI) has risen 70%, down from a first-half gain of 195%, Citi Newsroom reported, citing Databank.

In Kenya, Car & General (NSE:CGEN) leads the Nairobi Securities Exchange with a 400% gain to November 19, followed by the thinly traded Africa Mega Agricorp (NSE:AMAC), up 339%, insurer Britam (NSE:BRIT) at 98% and I&M Holdings (NSE:IMH) at 94%, according to AFX and African Financials data. The exchange operator itself, Nairobi Securities Exchange Plc (NSE:NSE), is up 78%; Nigerian Exchange Group recently bought a 10% stake in it. Kenya Airways (NSE:KQ) is up 53%, Equity Group (NSE:EQTY) 49%, KCB Group (NSE:KCB) 34% and Safaricom (NSE:SCOM), the largest listed company, 21%.

In Tanzania, Maendeleo Bank (DSE:MBP) has gained 161% and Vodacom Tanzania (DSE:VODA) 112%, while Tanga Cement (DSE:TCCL) and CRDB Bank (DSE:CRDB) are each up 82%, according to African Financials data to November 19. NMB Bank (DSE:NMB), whose shares were split in August, had a split-adjusted gain of 146% by the end of September, according to brokerage Alpha Capital.

In Uganda, Bank of Baroda Uganda (USE:BOBU) and Airtel Uganda (USE:AIRTEL) are both up 112%, Stanbic Bank Uganda (USE:SBU) 76%, Quality Chemical Industries (USE:QCIL) 49% and MTN Uganda (USE:MTNU) 44%. These figures exclude thinly traded cross-listed Kenyan stocks and penny stock National Insurance Corporation, which has risen from UGX5 to UGX25. Comparable stock-level figures for Rwanda were not available.

On the JSE, Sasol is the best-performing large company, up 93%, according to MarketScreener, although it has fallen almost 30% so far in November after peaking in late October. Shipping and logistics group Grindrod is up 55%, fertiliser and chemicals maker Omnia 54%, lifted by a R21.8bn takeover offer from Solar Group, and Aspen Pharmacare 53%. Gold and platinum miners have fallen as gold retreated from its January record: Sibanye-Stillwater is down 43%, Impala Platinum 34%, Harmony Gold 29% and Gold Fields 20%. Paper maker Sappi has lost 60% and retailer SPAR 43%.

In Egypt, small caps dominate the leaderboard. GlaxoSmithKline Egypt has gained 516%, International Co. for Investment & Development 269% and Arab Moltaqa Investments 250%. Among larger companies, Housing & Development Bank is up 142% and drugmaker Minapharm 121%.

In Morocco, where few stocks have risen, miners lead. Managem is up about 98%, adjusted for a ten-for-one share split in July, according to market data site Casabourse, while Compagnie Minière de Touissit CSE:CMT has gained 87%. Maroc Telecom (CSE:IAM), Morocco’s largest telecoms operator, is down 18%.

On the BRVM, banks lead. Coris Bank International (BRVM:CBIBF) has gained 168%, the Abidjan listing of Ecobank Transnational (BRVM:ETIT) 148% and Bank of Africa Burkina Faso (BRVM:BOABF) 107%, according to data site BRVM Data. The exchange’s composite index hit a then-record 555.48 points in mid-September, up about 61% for the year, before slipping about 10%, IntelliNews has reported.

In Zimbabwe, Tanganda Tea (ZSE:TANG) and TN CyberTech (ZSE:TNCI) have both risen more than 600% in local currency, though both trade thinly. Among larger companies, CBZ Holdings (ZSE:CBZ) is up 198% and Delta Corporation (ZSE:DLTA) 64%. On the dollar-denominated Victoria Falls Stock Exchange, crocodile-skin producer Padenga (VFEX:PHL) has gained 125%, Axia (VFEX:AXIA) 80%, Seed Co International (VFEX:SCIL) 71% and fast-food group Simbisa (VFEX:SIM) 59%, according to African Financials.

Elsewhere, Airtel Networks Zambia (LuSE:ATEL) is up 60% and Zanaco (LuSE:ZNCO) 42% in Lusaka. In Botswana, where the domestic index is almost flat, PrimeTime Property (BSE:PTPH) leads local companies with a 15% gain, while diamond miner Lucara (BSE:LUC) has lost 62%. In Mauritius, Afreximbank’s dollar-denominated depositary receipts are up 39% and hotel group Sun Ltd 13%, according to the Stock Exchange of Mauritius.

data.title: Copper heads for biggest weekly drop in 19 months as AI rout continues
data.description:
Copper slumped to its lowest since March on Friday and was on course for its steepest weekly drop in more than 19 months as appetite for investment in the AI sector continued to wane.

Benchmark three-month copper on the London Metal Exchange was down 1.7% at $12,310.50 per metric ton as of 1030 GMT. It earlier plunged as much as 4% to $12,202, its lowest since March 24.

The metal tipped to have a huge role in the AI infrastructure build-out is down around 8.2% this week, set for its steepest weekly fall since the week ended April 4, 2025.

"There's more and more evidence that the AI investment boom is waning and that the US Fed is going to have to get more aggressive with policy to control inflation," said Kyle Rodda, senior financial market analyst at Capital.com, adding that copper was being weighed down by a strengthening dollar .

One copper traded said the metal had been way oversold. "We can not live without AI," he said.

However, AI shares continued to sag, with Anthropic shares down 6% in premarket trading after a strong debut on Thursday.

On the physical side, there was slight relief in the recent tightness in China, where import premiums have hit record highs. Shanghai Futures Exchange copper stocks (CU-STX-SGH) rose by 3,204 tons over the past week to 30,846 tons - still less than a day's worth of Chinese consumption.

In the US, there was a rare delivery of 3,850 tons of copper into LME warehouses in Mobile, Alabama.

Meanwhile, the aluminium squeeze showed no signs of easing, with the premium of the cash LME contract over the three-month forward (CMAL0-3) last trading at a historical high of $323.50 a ton, indicating severe near-term supply shortages.

One entity holds 30%-39% of all LME aluminium warrants, LME data show.

data.title: Commerzbank CEO raises 2026 profit outlook as UniCredit takeover nears
data.description:
Commerzbank CEO Bettina Orlopp on Friday raised her profit outlook for 2026 as a takeover by UniCredit nears.

Orlopp, speaking at a financial conference, said the bank was now "clearly" expecting €3.5 billion ($3.8 billion) in net profit, more than a previous forecast of at least €3.4 billion.

She welcomed a broad agreement between the German government and UniCredit for providing clarity on key issues, including the bank's Frankfurt headquarters and stock market listing.

They were her first public remarks since the agreement was struck this week.

data.title: UK Borrowing Rises Less Than Forecast
data.description:
LONDON (dpa-AFX) - UK public sector net borrowing increased less than expected in October, the Office for National Statistics said Friday.

The government borrowed GBP 17.0 billion in October, which was up by GBP 0.8 billion from the last year. However, this was below the forecast of GBP 18.0 billion.

Central government debt interest payable climbed GBP 2.8 billion to GBP 11.2 billion in October.

In the financial year to October, borrowing dropped by GBP 7.3 billion to GBP 111.3 billion, equivalent to 3.5 percent of gross domestic product.

At the end of October, public sector net debt was provisionally estimated at GBP 3,058.3 billion, about GBP 161.6 billion more than in last year. Debt was equivalent to 95.8 percent of GDP.

data.title: Govt to expand Unified EV charging platform beyond five-state pilot as network strengthens
data.description:
The government will gradually expand the Unified Bharat e-Charge platform beyond its current pilot as the network becomes more reliable, Hanif Qureshi, Additional Secretary in the Ministry of Heavy Industries, said on Friday.

He said about 12 charging network operators had joined the platform, which lets electric vehicle (EV) users find, access and pay for charging across participating networks through a single interface.

“We have made it available for pilot testing in five states. As the network becomes more robust, we will keep expanding it,” Qureshi told reporters on the sidelines of the inaugural Growth and Readiness for EV Infrastructure Dialogue (GRID), organised by the Society of Indian Automobile Manufacturers (SIAM) as part of its National EV Charging Day event.

Qureshi said NPCI BHIM Services Ltd and Bharat Heavy Electricals Ltd (BHEL) developed the platform together. He said most manufacturers of electric two-wheelers, three-wheelers and four-wheelers had also been integrated. He gave no timeline for expanding the pilot.

The Ministry of Heavy Industries outlined the platform in May as a way for EV users to find and pay for charging across multiple operators through one interface. The ministry is also supporting the rollout of public charging infrastructure through a ₹2,000 crore allocation under the PM E-DRIVE scheme.

Asked about charging along national highways, Qureshi said they remained a priority. He said the government had identified 24 freight corridors and about 50 corridors for cars as priorities for electrification.

Qureshi said private operators could set up charging stations without a licence and that subsidies were available for areas where private investment was unlikely.

“Establishing a charging station is an unlicensed business. So, anybody can establish it,” he said, adding that operators were already setting up stations without government support.
